title: The Stag That Stopped
sceneText:
The stag comes into the afternoon light and stands in the clear ground between two oaks.

The best shot in the field already has it, and Baron Henk raises a hand.

He is keeping the chance back. Every year one stag is left for whoever the Baron thinks is worth a try.

Nobody is looking at the stag. They are looking at Henk, and Henk is looking at you.

Henk’s eyes come to rest on you for a second, and move off. He has not decided.

Beside you, Marguerite says quietly:

{@marguerite}“He is waiting for you.”

effects.logEntry: You stepped forward and took the stag.

choices.resultText:
You take one step forward.

Henk laughs at once, claps you hard on the back and holds out the gun. Somebody nearby says something and several of them laugh with him.

You raise it. The stag is still standing there, its head turned a little to one side, its ears moving.

From this distance it is larger than you had thought.

You fire. Whether the shot went home, nobody mentions again all day. The whole afternoon people come to talk to you. Somebody asks where you are from. Somebody asks how long you mean to stay at Maplegate. Somebody tells you a story about last year’s stag, at length.

On the ride back at dusk you understand that Henk has the trophy he wanted.

choices.text: Ask Marguerite quietly how Hartmann used to handle this moment

effects.logEntry: You quietly asked Marguerite how Hartmann used to handle this moment.

choices.resultText:
Her eyes go to the stag.

{@marguerite}“Every year he steps back behind somebody else, so that Henk cannot pick him.”

“Seven years of stepping back?”

{@marguerite}“Seven years,” she says. “The eighth he did not come.”

Ahead of you somebody else steps forward and takes the chance of the hunt.

Only then does Marguerite turn her head to look at you.

{@marguerite}“A person can keep out of the way of a thing for many years,” she says. “Keeping out of the way costs more than facing it, and what it costs runs out.”

choices.text: Stay where you are and do nothing

effects.logEntry: You stayed where you were and did not move.

choices.resultText:
You do not move.

Henk’s eyes rest on you once more, shorter this time than before, and go elsewhere.

Somebody else steps forward.

Things carry on. The noise comes back up, as though those few seconds had not happened.

Marguerite says nothing further.

For the rest of that day Henk is not cold to you; at supper he pours you wine and says two things about the weather.

He simply does not look at you again.
